quotes.quote: Refusal is only one third of willpower.
quotes.why: This is the chapter's strongest, most memorable compression of the core move.

quotes.quote: A goal must be present to have power.
quotes.why: This gives the mechanism in plain language and supports transfer beyond the examples.

quotes.quote: The safer move is to keep the run goal out of mind at the wrapper, because making a larger want present only strengthens the craving.
quotes.why: This reverses the chapter's own claim and damages the Brooklyn example.

quotes.quote: Self-control costs the comfort of staying vague.
quotes.why: This is a strong practical insight with a memorable consequence.

tells: Q1 choice c is the only option that mirrors the title-level three-part formula, so it is guessable from headings.
Q2 and Q9 repeat the prose/card phrase about goals biasing attention and response, making phrase matching enough.
Several distractors use extreme absolutes such as 'fake,' 'only,' 'no value,' or 'avoid cooperation,' making the moderate answer easy to spot.

complaints.problem: The What to do section first says Brooklyn should make the run goal present, then says the safer move is to keep it out of mind because making the larger want present strengthens craving; this is source-contradictory and misleading.

The intended answer is derivable from the chapter's main mechanism, but the Brooklyn source example contains contradictory advice, which makes the item less clean for a reader using the scene-specific evidence.
The phrase 'when your first habit is to call every lapse weak refusal' is compressed and less beginner-friendly than the rest of the chapter.
Several example explanations lean on repeated Miller/Cohen name-checking rather than showing a fresh before-to-after consequence, which lowers transfer even though the examples are usable.

parsedReview.oneParagraphVerdict: The chapter has a clear, teachable core: willpower is not just refusal but a three-part check of I will, I won't, and I want. The prose is concrete, memorable, and beginner-friendly, and most quiz answers are fair from the text. I would not ship it as-is against an 80-plus professional bar because Example 4 contains a direct contradiction of the central mechanism, and that contradiction spills into Q6. Fix that sentence and tighten a few overly easy distractors, and the chapter would be close.
